t:
It is the sense of Congress that—
    (1) in the report accompanying H.R. 1735 of the 114th Congress (House Report 114–102), the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives encouraged the Secretary of Defense to “publicly clarify the causes of the MV-22 mishap at Marana Northwest Regional Airport, Arizona, in a way consistent with the results of all investigations as soon as possible”; 
    (2) the Deputy Secretary of Defense Robert O. Work did an excellent job reviewing the investigations of such mishap and concluded that there was a misrepresentation of facts by the media which incorrectly identified pilot error as the cause of the mishap which the Deputy Secretary publicly made known in March 2016; and 
    (3) Congress is grateful for the successful conclusion to this tragic situation.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "publicly clarify" and the mention of the media bring the public into the process. But this is a sense-of-Congress statement about a past event involving only Congress and Defense Department officials, all inside the federal government. Telling the public the cause of a mishap is one-way disclosure, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives encouraged the Secretary of Defense to “publicly clarify the causes of the MV-22 mishap at Marana Northwest Regional Airport, Arizona, in a way consistent with the results of all investigations as soon as possible”

opus.w: The only interaction described is between a congressional committee and the Secretary of Defense, which stays entirely inside the federal government. Making a public clarification means the government informs the public; no outside party is consulted before a federal decision. The media appears only as the source of an earlier misstatement, so there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
opus.s: the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives encouraged the Secretary of Defense to “publicly clarify the causes of the MV-22 mishap at Marana Northwest Regional Airport, Arizona, in a way consistent with the results of all investigations as soon as possible”
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section quotes a House committee urging the Secretary to "publicly clarify" the cause of the mishap, and it mentions the media. That language sounds like it involves the public. It doesn't meet the definition. A House committee is inside the federal government. "Publicly clarify" means the government tells the public something; it doesn't ask outsiders for input. The media is mentioned only as the source of an earlier mistake, not as anyone taking part in a decision. The section is a sense-of-Congress statement that gives praise and thanks, and no federal decision depends on any outside input.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a 'sense of Congress' resolution expressing opinions and gratitude regarding past actions by federal officials. It does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. All entities mentioned (Congress, Secretary of Defense, Deputy Secretary of Defense) are inside the federal government, and no outside party is involved in a decision-making process.
